title: C# Questions & Answers - Basic Operation on Strings
sourceFile: Strings Basic Operation - C# Questions & Answers - Sanfoundry.html
description: This section of our 1000+ C# multiple choice questions focuses on basic operation on strings in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Which of the following String methods is used to compare two strings and determine their relative sort order?
questions.explanation: The 'CompareTo()' method compares the current string instance with another string and returns an integer that indicates whether the current instance precedes, follows, or occurs in the same position in the sort order.

questions.question: Choose the base class for the String type in C#:
questions.explanation: In C#, 'string' is an alias for the 'System.String' class, which is part of the .NET class library.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The Insert() method returns a new string. Inserting 'a' at index 2 of 'Cshr' results in 'Csahr'. Inserting 'p' at index 5 of 'Csahr' results in 'Csharp'.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about strings in C#?

options.text: The System.Array class is used to represent a string
A string has a zero-based index
A number cannot be represented in the form of a string
A string is mutable and can be modified directly

questions.explanation: Strings in C# are zero-indexed, meaning the first character is at index 0. They are immutable, not mutable.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: C# strings are case-sensitive. Both '==' and '.Equals()' compare the content of the strings. Since 'Hello' and 'hello' differ in casing, both comparisons return false.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The '+' operator is used for string concatenation in C#, joining the strings exactly as they are defined, including spaces.

questions.question: What is the correct way to find if the contents of two strings are equal in C#?
questions.explanation: In C#, the equality operator '==' is overloaded for the string type to compare the content (values) of the strings, not just their references.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct about C# strings?

options.text: String literals can contain escape sequences like '\n' or '\t'
Strings are fixed-size and stored on the stack

questions.explanation: C# strings are reference types, stored on the heap. They can contain any character literal, including escape sequences.

questions.question: Which of these operators can be used to concatenate two or more String objects?
questions.explanation: Both '+' (for joining strings in an expression) and '+=' (for appending to an existing string variable) can be used for concatenation.

questions.question: Which method is used to remove all leading and trailing white-space characters from a string?
questions.explanation: The 'Trim()' method removes both leading and trailing white space. 'TrimStart()' only removes white space from the beginning of the string.
